title: Lumen feedback raft & quickpatch notes
body:
Context:
- Purpose: collect fast-moving customer signal from last 6 weeks, surface low-effort patches we can ship in the next 1–3 sprints, and record tradeoffs/owner. This is a working notebook (Lumen raft) — intentionally rough.
- Inputs: weekly CS digs, triage Slack thread #cs-feedback, three customer calls (Acme Retail, Docflow AI, FinSage), recent SLO/latency anomalies, KV-cache telemetry.

Method / framing:
- Prioritize: (1) user-facing breakages that block production, (2) high-frequency friction with low dev cost, (3) architectural changes flagged by multiple accounts.
- Quickpatch = <= 5 dev-days + simple rollout (feature flag/canary).
- Estimate impact using heuristics: frequency (low/med/high), severity (nuisance/blocker), revenue sensitivity (low/med/high).

Raw vignettes (paraphrased):
1) Acme Retail — "Token explosion when generating product descriptions for long catalogs; sometimes generation stalls mid-stream and we see client retries — costs spike." (saw on 2026-05-05; frequency: med; ticket CS-4821)
2) Docflow AI — "Embeddings drift after a model swap; similarity searches return weird top results until we rebuild embedding index; no rollback path for older embeddings." (saw on 2026-05-11; frequency: low; revenue sens: med)
3) FinSage — "Occasional 502s when routing to the cheaper model variant during bursts; prefer predictable latency even if cost a little higher." (saw on 2026-05-13; frequency: med; severity: blocker during batch jobs)

Observed patterns / recurring signals:
- KV-cache warmup pain: several customers report a warmup window after cold-starts and after model rollouts where prefix caching is ineffective — leads to latency spikes and retry loops.
- Model-variant routing friction: fallback rules are too permissive in some tenant configs, causing noisier cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Embedding indexing/compatibility is fragile across small model version changes; tooling for compatibility checks is missing.
- Streaming completeness: clients sometimes see partial streams when a transient GPU OOM occurs; no graceful retry orchestration.

Top quickpatch candidates (ranked):
A) KV-cache soft-warmup shim (owner: eng-serving-runtime, owner: Ravi)
- What: On cold model activation, keep a short-lived conservative batch size + proactive small prefix priming for top N requests seen in the last hour.
- Why: reduces mid-run latency spikes and client retries (addresses Acme + others).
- Dev cost: ~3 dev-days to prototype + 1 day rollout gating flag.
- Impact: frequency=high, severity=med, estimated token-cost savings on retries: 12–25% for affected tenants.
- Risks: slightly higher initial cost on priming; must guard against priming toxic prompts.
- Linked ticket: RUNTIME-934.

B) Safer routing fallback policy (owner: product-hosted-api, owner: Maya)
- What: Add a tenant-level override to prefer latency-stable variants; introduce a throttle window for variant-switching during bursts.
- Why: FinSage 502s and unpredictable fallbacks.
- Dev cost: ~5 dev-days (policy + UI toggle + tests).
- Impact: frequency=med, severity=high for some tenants.
- Rollout: feature-flag + 2-week canary.

C) Embedding compatibility audit tool + auto-tagging (owner: applied-ml, owner: Samir)
- What: lightweight preflight check that computes a small compatibility score when a model change is requested and flags rebuild necessity. Auto-tag embedding jobs by model-version.
- Dev cost: ~4 dev-days for audit + 2 for tagging in indexer.
- Impact: prevents Docflow drift; frequency=low but high-cost when it occurs.

D) Streaming retry orchestration (owner: site-reliability-engineering, owner: TBD)
- What: when an in-flight stream fails due to transient OOM, attempt an automated resume from last stable token using request-level checkpointing (best-effort).
- Dev cost: 8–12 dev-days (complex).
- Impact: high user perceived reliability; not a quickpatch but important for roadmap.

Lightweight mitigation sketches / playbook entries (can be executed by CS + SE):
- Customer-specific workaround email template for embedding drift (how to force index rebuild, small shell commands, recommended model pinning).
- Docs update: recommended routing policy examples (latency-first vs cost-first) with decision trees and cost/latency graphs.
- Trial canary: for 2 affected tenants offer to pin to dedicated pool for 48 hours and collect traces.

Cost / effort vs impact (summary):
- KV-cache shim: low effort, broad impact — recommend prioritize for next sprint.
- Safer routing fallback: medium effort, targeted but critical for paying enterprise customers — schedule concurrent with KV shim.
- Embedding audit: medium effort, high value for customers with heavy vector indexes — schedule after routing fix or as parallel spike.
- Streaming orchestration: larger workstream; add to Q3 roadmap.

Unresolved questions / risks:
- How to safely prime KV-cache without leaking sensitive prompt content? (privacy guardrails needed).
- Do we want tenant-level default preference or org-wide? (product & sales input required)
- Are there billing implications for priming/extra token consumption? (finance ops check).

Next steps / action items (owner in parentheses):
1) Kick off 3-day spike for KV-cache shim: infra + runtime to prototype (Ravi) — target: demo by 2026-05-28.
2) Product to draft routing fallback toggle UI text and canary plan (Maya) — target: 2026-06-04.
3) CS to send embedding rebuild playbook + two-customer offer for index rebuild assistance (Aisha) — target: 2026-05-24.
4) Create unified incident tag for "kv-warmup" across SLO alerts so we can measure incidence (SRE) — target: 2026-05-27.

Decision log (brief):
- 2026-05-21: Prioritized KV-cache shim (fastest path to reduce retries).
- 2026-05-25: Approved routing fallback feature-flag UX scope (product).

Notes to self / scratches:
- Keep samples of problematic prompts anonymized and attached to RUNTIME-934.
- Check if dedicated customers are being billed for priming tokens; flag to finance.

Appendix: quick reference links and snippets
- Observability query samples (SLOs): "latency_p50, p95 by tenant where kv_hits=0 and request_age < 2h"
- Useful logs: recent Acme traces: trace IDs 0a1b2c3d.. (stored in S3 /traces/2026-05/).
- Small list of follow-up meetings: 2026-05-22 10:00 (runtime spike sync), 2026-05-26 16:00 (product routing review).

End of Lumen raft — this doc is a living artifact. Add notes below when you triage or pick up an action.
